items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: When I hear that, like Bryan Adams, Tears for Fears, whatever that, heavy reverb on two and four, and those synths, it’s so nostalgic to me.

ctx.x: Yeah. And also in the mid 80s the rap music started to become quite popular and I just wondered if that entered your consciousness. Because you’re so, you’re such a percussive guy.

I am yeah. It’s funny, well I didn’t always get into rap when I was younger mainly because my parents would not have approved. And I was very much a goody two shoes. You know I talked about wanting to please people, I really wanted to please my parents. It worked for me. I was happy that way, not kind of like stretching the boundaries when I was a kid, though we did listen to — I would often just say, just all the pop music we listened to, the 80s pop, 90s pop, where there’s always a backbeat on two and four,…

dance, experiencing all these things, that’s the soundtrack of your growing up. And it’s like life is too short to like move beyond that. And I’ve learned to just embrace it. It’s okay. I like the stuff and it’s okay if this enters my playing. Yeah.
